A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FOCUS research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic ridge-regression experiments and CIFAR-10 classification experiments, including results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains these original ridge-regression and CIFAR-10 experiments, with the classification results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: The core FOCUS and SG-FOCUS updates are retained. However, Algorithm 2 replaces v1's explicit zero stored-gradient initialization with equality to a client tracker whose initial value is unclear before its subsequent reset. The PDFs do not resolve whether this changes initialization or is an incomplete notational rewrite.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic ridge regression under full, uniform, and arbitrary participation, and heterogeneous CIFAR-10 classification under active and passive arbitrary participation. No dataset or evaluated scenario is added.

E2.justification: The ridge-regression comparators remain FedAvg, FedAU, SCAFFOLD, and ProxSkip. The CIFAR-10 comparators remain FedAU and SCAFFOLD in both participation scenarios.

E3.justification: Reported settings match: ridge regression uses d=100, N=16, K=100, lambda=0.01, tau=5, and learning rate 0.0002. CIFAR-10 retains the three-layer CNN, 32 clients, three local updates, 10,000 rounds, learning rate 0.002, and Dirichlet alpha=0.05. Metrics and testing procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The participation-regime comparisons and heterogeneous-data illustration are retained. No new ablation, sensitivity study, robustness test, or error analysis appears. The new Markov-participation discussion does not report a corresponding experiment.

E5.justification: Both versions present the same experimental curves and neither documents empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Added expectations in theoretical statements are not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The ridge-regression curves in v1 Figure 5 and v2 Figure 4 are identical, as are the CIFAR-10 curves in Figure 9. Reported empirical rankings, convergence trends, and accuracy findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 adds expectations to the main PL/nonconvex bounds and makes Lemma 3 conditional. It also changes the main Lyapunov coefficient from kappa to tau and the nonconvex summand's iterate index from r to R, without matching revisions in Appendices D.5/D.7. The theorem families and underlying proof arguments are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first proof of exact linear convergence under arbitrary participation. Its abstract omits v1's strongly-convex/PL qualification, although the main theorem retains those restrictions. The central FOCUS and SG-FOCUS contributions otherwise remain.

C2.justification: New Section 5.3 states that the proof does not cover Markov-dependent participation and distinguishes believed convergence in that setting from established guarantees. v1 lacks this qualification. The existing delayed-gradient interpretation and empirical explanations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix F.1 adds a statement that implementation code is supplied with supplementary material; v1 has no such access statement. Neither supplied PDF embeds that code, so its actual availability cannot be verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Defazio et al. (2014), Horn and Johnson (2012), Meyer (2023), Nguyen et al. (2025), and Wang et al. (2020), while removing Stich (2018), Li et al. (2020), and Li et al. (2024). These are limited citation and positioning changes within the retained FL/push-pull framework.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially rewritten. Graph modeling receives a separate section, algorithm development and performance analysis are reorganized, and the decentralized review and FedAvg theorem move into appendices. An appendix contents list is added.

P2.justification: Document-wide typography, margins, title/author presentation, and equation/algorithm layout change. Table 1 moves into the introduction, the DGD illustration moves into an appendix, and graphics are resized and repositioned. The experimental graphics themselves retain identical content.

improvement.justification: v2 improves navigation, expands algorithm explanations, and adds a useful limitation on Markov-dependent participation. However, new coefficient and iterate-index discrepancies in Theorem 1 conflict with Appendices D.5/D.7, while the abstract drops the function-class qualification on linear convergence. These accessibility and transparency gains coexist with reduced precision in central guarantees, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
